design: 4 authentic operator questions × 2 conditions × 2 models (claude sonnet, claude opus). raw: read-only agent over docs/decisions + docs/trust/trust-claims.yml only. graph: the experimenter chose the matching named view from views.json by hand and supplied the deterministic premises selectView returned (node ids, kinds, roles, statuses, statements, typed edges); the agent could also read ADRs for rationale. This is ARM 2 of the doc's comparison (today's flat named-view catalog) against ARM 1 (raw corpus). No operator family or qualifier was invoked, so arms 3–5 were NOT run and this record says nothing about the candidate grammar. Cross-provider consistency was not measured — both models are one provider.

questions.Q-a: If the fixed six-step pipeline and the two separate review orchestrators were removed tomorrow, what architectural intent must survive, and what is free to change? (view: affected source=ADR-0022)
questions.Q-b: What would have to be true for provider-diverse review to no longer be worth its cost, and what evidence would show it? (view: review)
questions.Q-c: The landing executor is being replaced. What must remain true for landing to be safe regardless of the new mechanism? (view: landing)
questions.Q-d: Which recorded decisions are historical, superseded, or under reconsideration rather than current, and what current intent did each serve? (premises: all decisions)

judge: realizationAsIntent counts must-survive items that name a concrete mechanism (CAS push, --force-with-lease, worktree, parkExit, codegen/verify interleave, seat configuration) rather than a property; judged by the session author, not a model — a known limitation.

graph.questions: Q-a, Q-b, Q-c (arm 2 vs arm 1); Q-d excluded

raw.questions: Q-a, Q-b, Q-c (arm 2 vs arm 1); Q-d excluded

defectsInTheGraphSurfacedByTheRun: supersedes was a declared relation with zero edges; the graph-condition opus replica on Q-d noted that DEC-0015 over DEC-0002 lived only in ADR-0025 prose. Authored (encoding-loss bucket: authoring-cost gap)

DEC-0012 carried status 'historical-topology-under-reconsideration' with no source. Both RAW replicas on Q-d found ADR-0022 accepted and unamended and did not list it; both GRAPH replicas repeated the label. Relabelled current-construction-choice and logged as an extraction.openQuestions entry (the graph overclaimed — the inverse of encoding loss, which the source-grounding check cannot catch, and which the raw condition caught)

confounds: the matching view (affected/review/landing/all-decisions) was selected by the experimenter, not by a model normalizing the question — that is the probabilistic half the contract leaves outside the deterministic seam, and its cost is not in the table

graph Jaccard is over the node ids bracketed in items, which is a smaller set than the item count (an item may cite two ids; two items may cite one); raw Jaccard is over concepts hand-mapped by the experimenter
the experimenter judged realizationAsIntent for both conditions after seeing which condition produced each answer
no recall measure: fewer must-survive items under the graph condition may be tighter boundedness or intent the bounded premise set omitted — represented-fact completeness was not scored
graph Jaccard is over a closed, experimenter-supplied id set; raw Jaccard over open-ended hand-mapped concepts — the units differ and the comparison is biased toward the graph condition
the reconciled Q-a agreement (1.00) is obtained by dropping DEC-0012, whose double classification traces to the unsourced status this run itself exposed
Q-b is challenge-shaped (a defeater of ASM-0002), not recover-shaped; no family was invoked in any run

doubleClassifiedIds.note: a bracketed id is a citation, not a classification; where an id appears on both sides the item text on the must-survive side names an invariant and the id is its implementing decision or governing constraint. Reconciled Jaccard drops those ids from the must-survive set.
